https://english.news.cn/20260719/946d04a.text: Hungarian president signs constitutional amendment ending own mandate Source: Xinhua Editor: huaxia 2026-07-19 01:56:30 BUDAPEST, July 18 (Xinhua) -- Hungarian President Tamas Sulyok on Saturday signed the country's 17th constitutional amendment, triggering the end of his mandate as head of state. Once the law is published in the official gazette, the termination of his mandate will take effect the following day. In a video statement, Sulyok said he had signed the amendment because he had "no constitutional means of acting against this amendment, which violates constitutional principles but was adopted by the National Assembly (parliament) ... through a lawful procedure." Prime Minister Peter Magyar welcomed the signing, saying it had "removed the last obstacle to implementing our joint decisions." He said he would consult parliamentary parties on a successor, adding that "the moral basis of the nomination can only come from the trust of society." Sulyok was elected by Hungary's then Fidesz-majority parliament in 2024 for a five-year term, with his mandate originally due to expire in March 2029. However, Magyar has repeatedly called on Sulyok to resign, accusing him of serving the interests of the previous Fidesz government. The constitutional amendment ending Sulyok's mandate was adopted by parliament earlier this week after Magyar's ruling party secured the two-thirds majority needed to amend the constitution. Under the constitution, parliament must elect a new president by secret ballot within 30 days. Any Hungarian citizen aged 35 or older is eligible for the office if nominated by at least one-fifth of lawmakers, or 40 members of parliament. Until a new president takes office, presidential duties will be exercised by Speaker of Parliament Agnes Forsthoffer. The new head of state will assume office on the eighth day after the election result is officially announced. Magyar has said he wants to nominate a candidate capable of representing the unity of the nation and winning support from opposition lawmakers, although he has not yet named a candidate. He has also said the latest constitutional amendment is intended as a temporary arrangement and that Hungary will eventually introduce direct presidential elections under a new constitution to be approved by referendum. ■

(Photo: AFP) International News , Latest News July 19, 2026 Influencer Andrew Tate and brother arrested in Miami WASHINGTON, United States (AFP) — Radical social media influencer Andrew Tate and his brother Tristan were in custody in the US on Sunday, officials said, as Britain seeks their extradition to face new charges of rape, sex trafficking and assault. Karena Thomas, assistant chief constable of the United Kingdom’s (UK) Bedfordshire Police, said the pair had been detained “pending ongoing legal proceedings”. The US Marshals Service confirmed the arrests. US news outlet TMZ posted video of law enforcement officers placing the self-professed misogynist and his younger sibling in handcuffs and escorting them into waiting vehicles in Miami on Saturday. Asked by an onlooker if he had something to say, Tristan Tate did not respond, the footage posted on X showed. UK prosecutors, who are now due to seek the brothers’ extradition, said the arrests came after they brought forward 38 further charges against the pair. The Tate brothers now face 59 charges in total — 42 against Andrew and 17 against Tristan, British authorities said on Sunday. “We have decided to prosecute Andrew and Tristan Tate for further offences including rape, arranging or facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation and offences relating to indecent images of a child,” Malcolm McHaffie, head of UK’s Crown Prosecution Service’s (CPS) Special Crime Division, said in a statement. “The CPS has requested the extradition of the Tates from the US,” he said, adding that the latest charges stem from receipt of new evidence from Bedfordshire Police that bring the total number of alleged victims in the Tates case to seven. Earlier this year, police in Hertfordshire, north of London, said they were reopening a probe into rape and sexual assault allegations made by women against Andrew Tate between 2014 and 2015. They also face separate rape and human trafficking allegations brought by different women and investigated by Bedfordshire Police, which covers their hometown of Luton, also north of London. The Tate brothers are also accused of tax evasion and money laundering in the UK. Their attorney, Joseph McBride, said in a press release that the brothers “are innocent”. “We are confident that once a competent judge sees the facts, and once the Department of Justice confronts this egregious abuse of its own authority, Andrew and Tristan Tate will walk free,” McBride said. The Tates are dual British-US citizens who have been avid supporters of US President Donald Trump. Lawyer Matt Jury, of McCue Jury & Partners who represent four alleged British victims of Andrew Tate, said Tate was “now facing the real prospect of extradition to the UK after years of public campaigning by the four British women I represent”. “They have spent years fighting for action to be taken, and I now urge the authorities to ensure this case proceeds as quickly as possible. “Andrew and Tristan Tate are accused of some of the most serious offences, including multiple counts of rape and human trafficking. It is time they face justice,” he was quoted by the PA news agency as saying. In March 2025, the US state of Florida launched a criminal investigation against them. The status of that investigation is unclear. Andrew Tate is one of the most prominent proponents of the so-called “manosphere” network of communities, many of them online, that focus on traditional masculinity, anti-feminism and self-improvement. He promotes his divisive views, often incorporating alpha-male and aggressively misogynistic themes, to millions on social media including 10.8 million followers on X. In Romania, where they have been based in recent years, the Tates face allegations of trafficking minors, sexual intercourse with a minor and money laundering. https://www.newswise.com/articles/roger-.text: Roger S. Foster, Jr., MD, FACS, and Baiba J. Grube, MD, FACS, Are the ACS Foundation Distinguished Philanthropists of the Year Newswise — WASHINGTON (September 28, 2026) — The American College of Surgeons (ACS) Foundation announced Roger S. Foster, Jr., MD, FACS, and Baiba J. Grube, MD, FACS, as the recipients of its prestigious Distinguished Philanthropist Award, which was presented during the ACS Clinical Congress 2026 in Washington, DC. The award recognizes the married couple's exemplary investment in the mission of the ACS and surgical care worldwide. The Distinguished Philanthropist Award, established in 1989, celebrates outstanding individuals who have significantly supported the ACS Foundation's mission to advance surgical practices, research, and patient care. "Dr. Foster and Dr. Grube's generosity is a powerful force for progress in surgery, but it is their unique combination of philanthropic support and hands-on leadership that truly sets them apart," said H. Randolph Bailey, MD, FACS, Chair of the ACS Foundation. "Their dedication to advancing surgical oncology, trauma care, and surgical education, backed by their own clinical experience, has left an indelible mark on the ACS and the patients we all serve." For both Dr. Foster and Dr. Grube, the recognition capped long and productive surgical careers and highlighted a selfless focus on the wellbeing of the ACS. Dr. Foster enjoyed a career as a leader in surgical oncology. He earned his medical degree at Case Western Reserve University, then completed surgical residency at University Hospitals of Cleveland in Ohio and a fellowship at Roswell Park Memorial Institute in Buffalo, New York. A drive to research brought him to the University of Vermont in Burlington, where he began surgical practice as an assistant professor. As his career gained recognition, he participated in eleven National Cancer Institute committees and chaired the Cancer Clinical Investigations Review Committee. He retired as the Wadley R. Glenn Professor of Surgery at Emory University and Chief of Surgical Services at Emory's Crawford Long Hospital in Atlanta, Georgia. His leadership included significant contributions to the ACS. Dr. Foster served as secretary of the Vermont chapter, participated in nearly a dozen ACS committees, joined the Board of Governors, and became a member of the Board of Regents for 9 years, where he served on the Executive Committee of the Board of Regents for 6 of those years. He also holds a rare distinction: a connection by marriage to an ACS founder. Dr. Foster met George W. Crile, Jr., MD, FACS, and his family during his first year in medical school. Joan Crile and Dr. Foster married after his third year of medical school. Joan's active support of his career began with his research activities during his first two medical school summers. George W. Crile, Jr., MD, FACS, was a son of George W. Crile, MD, FACS, who co-founded the Cleveland Clinic and the ACS. Dr. Foster later married Dr. Crile's daughter, Joan, making him a grandson-in-law of the ACS founder. Four years after his wife's death in 2000, after his wife's death in 2000, Dr. Foster remarried to Baiba Grube, MD, FACS. The two first encountered each other at the University of Vermont, where Dr. Grube completed her surgical residency and where Dr. Foster served as one of her research mentors. A native of Albany, New York, Dr. Grube attended medical school at the University of Utah in Salt Lake City. She completed a fellowship in trauma and burn care at Harborview Medical Center in Seattle, then retrained in surgical oncology at the City of Hope in Duarte, California, and completed supplemental education in breast oncology at the John Wayne Cancer Institute. She retired from surgery in 2011 from Yale University in New Haven, Connecticut. Drs. Foster and Grube are dedicated, generous philanthropists. Dr. Grube has donated to Latvian social and cultural organizations, the Association of Women Surgeons, The Scripps Research Institute, University of Utah Medical School, University of Texas Medical Branch, and New England Surgical Society, and music organizations. Dr. Foster has focused on the universities that touched his life: Haverford College, Case Western Reserve University, and the University of Vermont. Together, they established the Foster Family Scholarship Fund at Haverford College to alleviate undergraduate students' financial need, and The Roger S. Foster, Jr., MD, Catamount Surgeon Visiting Professorship at the University of Vermont. They are both amateur musicians, Baiba piano and Roger cello, and they have been particularly supportive of the Lake Champlain Chamber Music Festival, where Roger served as Chairman of the Board for five years. Their strongest interest, however, may be the ACS. "I lived all my life as a participant in the field of surgery, and those hours were greater than hours spent with family or with friends. So, it's important to give back to our professional family, just like you support your children or you support your parents or relatives," Dr. Grube explained. Their gifts to the ACS Foundation have been unrestricted, permitting the College flexibility to use the funds where they are needed most. "I want a strong organization to be able to go the way they need to go," Dr. Foster said. Asked about their own legacies, both expressed little concern, instead saying the wellbeing of the College was their chief interest. "It's the future generations of the College to impact and support them in the best way possible," Dr. Foster said. "The legacy should be the College," Dr. Grube concurred. # # # About the American College of Surgeons The American College of Surgeons (ACS) is a scientific and educational organization of surgeons that was founded in 1913 to raise the standards of surgical practice and improve the quality of care for all surgical patients. The ACS is dedicated to the ethical and competent practice of surgery. Its achievements have significantly influenced the course of scientific surgery in America and have established it as an important advocate for all surgical patients. The ACS has approximately 95,000 members and is the largest organization of surgeons in the world. “FACS” designates that a surgeon is a Fellow of the ACS. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c6x2.text: Image source, Reuters Image caption, Warehouses, railway stations, energy plants and residential buildings were hit during a night of heavy Russian strikes By Dan Woodland Â and Â Sarah Rainsford ,Â Eastern and Southern Europe correspondent, in Kyiv Published 20 November 2026, 08:04 GMT Updated 13:01 GMT Russia targeted bridges in Kyiv and railway stations overnight in a major attack launched days after Ukraine badly damaged the strategically important Crimean Bridge. Ballistic missiles hit key crossings in the capital during a nationwide assault which Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said was "one of the most massive strikes" of the war so far and left at least nine dead. Russian President Vladimir Putin had threatened to retaliate for the attack on the Crimean Bridge, which the Kremlin built to link Russia and the occupied Crimean peninsula. The latest Russian strikes coincided with talks around the war, and came as the Kremlin pushed back against a US claim that Russia could be open to Western-backed security guarantees for Ukraine. The overnight attack against Ukraine was spread across several cities and regions, Zelensky said, with residential buildings and energy facilities also hit. Air raid sirens lasted non-stop throughout the night and were ongoing into the morning. Zelensky said over 110 missiles and more than 400 attack drones were launched by Russia, adding that "particularly insidious" tactics to launch the waves in 20 to 30-minute internals made it "more difficult to extinguish fires, clear debris, and restore services". The three bridges targeted in Kyiv - the Podilsko-Voskresensky Bridge, the Darnytskyi Bridge and the Southern Bridge - were closed to traffic. Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko urged people to "avoid travelling into the city by private car unless absolutely necessary", adding to the disruption around the capital following a first round of strikes against vital crossings earlier this week. At least seven people were killed and 17 more were injured, Klitschko added, with unspecified civilian facilities also hit. Ukraine's major operation to take out the road section of the Crimean Bridge earlier this week was a tactical and symbolic blow for Moscow. Since illegally annexing Crimea in 2014, Moscow has housed troops and military equipment there, with occupying forces travelling through the peninsula towards the front line. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said an operation to weaken the bridge's defences and ultimately cause part of it to collapse had been weeks in the making. Russian President Vladimir Putin - who personally opened the bridge in 2019 to international condemnation - said the Kremlin's retaliation for the strike would be "far more painful". Of the nine fatalities confirmed so far, seven were in Kyiv and two were in Lviv, with at least 28 people injured. The Sknyliv railway station in Lviv, a city in western Ukraine which has become one of the primary entry points to Ukraine for people and international aid, was badly damaged, the city's Mayor Andriy Sadovyi said. Image source, AFP via Getty Images Image caption, At least two people were killed in a strike on a railway station in western Ukraine The attack began hours after European leaders including UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham, French President Emmanuel Macron and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said they were ready for negotiations involving Moscow to end the war in Ukraine. The Berlin meeting of the so-called coalition of the willing, an international alliance of Ukraine's allies committed to providing security support in the event of a peace deal, was attended by Zelensky and US President Donald Trump's envoys. Jared Kushner said the US "wants to make a deal with Europe by his side" after fears of an agreement negotiated between the US and Russia were reignited by Trump's one-to-one talks with Putin earlier this week. He claimed Russia was "comfortable" with Ukraine having security guarantees based on Nato's Article Five, which requires allies to come to a country's defence if it comes under attack. On Monday, Russia's deputy foreign minister Sergei Ryabkov pushed back against that, saying "quasi-Nato" membership for Ukraine would be "unacceptable" to Russia. The Kremlin has long cited the prospect of Ukraine joining Nato as a key justification for its war effort. The US president dialled into the Berlin talks from Air Force One on his way back from China, where he met his Russian counterpart and Chinese leader Xi Jinping. He reportedly questioned the decision of European leaders to commit â¬70bn (Â£58.6bn; $76.bn) in military funding for Ukraine. The UK and France are jointly leading the first military exercise organised by the coalition of the willing, which involves thousands of troops from 11 countries and is taking place in Poland. On Friday, Poland's Prime Minister Donald Tusk accused Russia of an "intentional provocation" after a Russian cruise missile landed in his country . It struck around 50km (31 miles) from its border with Ukraine, the Polish Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz said on Friday. Two more unidentified projectiles, suspected to be a drone and a second missile, landed in villages nearby and no one was harmed, he added. Polish and Swedish jets were scrambled on Nato's eastern flank as Russia's attack on western Ukraine continued. They have since been stood down. France's foreign minister Jean-NoÃ«l Barro has called for a meeting of the UN Security Council following Russia's attack on Kyiv. He described the strikes, which reportedly damaged the Austrian and Dutch embassies, as "crimes" that "Russia will have to answer for".
